name: NETHERLANDS
lead: The Netherlands is small and flat. A quarter of its land is below sea level. The Dutch built huge dykes to keep the sea out. Tulip fields blaze with colour every spring, and canals thread through Amsterdam.

sections.geography: A land won from the sea

geo: The land is so flat you can cycle for days without a hill. Polders are old seabed drained by dykes and pumps. The Rhine and Maas rivers fan out into a delta.
Gentle hills rise near Vaalserberg in the south. The Wadden Sea coast is a UNESCO site. The sea empties and fills twice a day. Sandbanks crowd with birds and basking seals.
animals: Thousands of grey seals rest on Wadden Sea sandbanks. White storks return each spring to nest on rooftops and poles. Villagers think they bring good luck.
European badgers dig their homes in the wooded east. Stocky grey Konik horses roam wild in reserves like Oostvaardersplassen.
culture: The Dutch say exactly what they mean. It avoids confusion. Cycling is simply life here: 23 million bikes for 18 million people.
Dutch food is hearty. People eat stroopwafels (waffle-and-caramel sandwiches), raw herring from street stalls and Gouda cheese. The Dutch also gave the world Rembrandt, Vermeer and Van Gogh.
history: In the 1600s the Dutch were the world's richest traders. Amsterdam was the busiest port on Earth. The Dutch East India Company was the first company anyone could buy shares in.
Nazi occupation in World War II caused the terrible Hunger Winter of 1944–45. The Dutch later built a modern welfare state and co-founded NATO and the European Union.
wows: Without dykes, much of Amsterdam would sit under water.
There are more bicycles than people in the Netherlands.
The Dutch export over a billion tulip bulbs every year.
Schiphol Airport sits on a drained lake bed, about 3 metres below sea level.
Rotterdam is Europe's biggest port, handling over 400 million tonnes of cargo a year.
Dutch people are among the tallest in the world.
Sint Maarten, a small Caribbean island, is shared by the Dutch and the French.

myths.fact: Holland is only two provinces in the west. The whole country has twelve provinces.
Modern electric pumps do the work now. Historic windmills are preserved landmarks; a few still grind grain, but none manage flood control today.
